body.question: Most data between continents travels under the sea or through space?
options: Under the sea, by fibre cable
body.reveal: Cables can carry far more data at a fraction of the cost of satellites. It is hard to say exactly, but satellites are a very small share: FCC statistics put them at just 0.37% of US international capacity. For most of the crossing, a cable is about as wide as a garden hose.

probes.question: What share of US international capacity do satellites account for, per FCC statistics?
True or false: for most of its journey a submarine cable is typically as wide as a garden hose.
